system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}

CONCEPT: atomic_ref

ATOM DPCPP2-C03-S3-03 (S3): Atomicity guarantees do not apply if only some of the concurrent accesses to a memory location use atomics, and mixing atomic and non-atomic operations on the same location at the same time results in undefined behavior.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0551-s04] Note that this guarantee does not apply if only some of the accesses use atomics and that it is our responsibility as programmers to ensure that we do not concurrently access the same data using operations with different atomicity guarantees.
[DPCPP2-p0551-s05] Mixing atomic and non-atomic operations on the same memory location(s) at the same time results in undefined behavior!

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Separately asserts loss of atomicity guarantees and undefined behavior from concurrent mixed access. / Joins two claims: atomicity guarantees do not apply on mixed access, and concurrent mixed access causes undefined behavior.
- L1_ONLY: hold — Retain the undefined-behavior rule and remove the additional assertion about atomicity guarantees.

The separate claim that atomicity guarantees do not apply under mixed access was removed."}
